question: cust is at the counter wanting to return unopened amoxicilin they bought yesterday, still has receipt. can we refund?
text:
Questions about returns, refunds, stock, sales, storage, expiry and product leaflets are pharmacy work, so rule 2 never applies to them.

Source [returns_and_expiry_policy.md#Customer-Returns] (Customer Returns)
Return decisions are made at the counter and apply in the same way at every branch.

1. Prescription medications cannot be returned or refunded once they have left the pharmacy counter. This includes all antibiotics, such as amoxicillin, even when the box is unopened and the customer has the receipt.
2. A dispensed prescription item is eligible for replacement only when it is damaged or is covered by a manufacturer recall.
3. Unopened over-the-counter (OTC) items and vitamins with an intact tamper seal and the original receipt may be returned or exchanged within 7 calendar days of the purchase date.
4. Cold-chain items and prescription drugs are excluded from this return period.

If a return cannot be accepted, explain the reason politely, and offer to ask the supervising pharmacist to speak with the customer.

Source [storage_sop.md#Cold-Chain-And-Excursions] (Cold Chain And Excursions)
Cold-chain products, including vaccines, must be stored in the designated refrigerator. The acceptable cold-chain storage range is 2°C–8°C. An excursion is any period in which the recorded temperature is outside 2°C–8°C.

For any excursion lasting longer than 30 minutes, staff must:

1. Tag all affected stock "DO NOT DISPENSE - QUARANTINE" and keep it in the refrigerator.
2. Record the peak temperature and the duration of the excursion in the temperature log.
3. Notify the supervising pharmacist before any unit is sold or dispensed.

Do not discard affected stock. The supervising pharmacist decides whether it can be released or must be returned or destroyed. An excursion of 30 minutes or less is still written in the temperature log.

Source [storage_sop.md#Receiving-And-FEFO] (Receiving And FEFO)
Every delivery is inspected at the time it arrives, before it is put away.

1. Check the delivery against the order for product, quantity and batch number.
2. Check each package for damage, and check the expiry date of every batch. Reject any item that is damaged or already expired.
3. Cold-chain items go into the refrigerator immediately.

question: does the paracetamol leaflet say anything about drinking alcohol or taking cold meds at the same time?
text:
Drinking alcohol while taking paracetamol can increase the risk of liver toxicity. If you drink alcohol regularly and heavily, consult a doctor or pharmacist before taking paracetamol [paracetamol_leaflet.md#Warnings-And-Precautions].

Taking cold or flu remedies containing paracetamol with other paracetamol-containing products can cause an accidental overdose and severe liver damage (hepatotoxicity) [paracetamol_leaflet.md#Warnings-And-Precautions].

Combining paracetamol with other medications, including cold and flu remedies, is not recommended without consulting a doctor or pharmacist [paracetamol_leaflet.md#Dosage-And-Administration].

It is recommended to check the ingredients on the label of every cold or flu product before use, and to consult a doctor or pharmacist if you are unsure about any interactions [paracetamol_leaflet.md#Warnings-And-Precautions].
